content.text: Investigation complete. The only termination-payment mechanic is in § 4(a), and it is an entitlement to actual fees generated during the notice period — not a liquidated or penal sum.

input.quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee-on-termination or early-termination fee payable by AP, so the preferred position ("Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties") is met on the face of the document. The only termination-related payment mechanic, § 4(a), entitles Kubient to "all fees generated during the termination period" — i.e. its actual revenue share on fees actually generated during the 90-day notice period, not a pre-agreed sum untethered to performance; it is not triggered by minor breach and is expressly disapplied on termination for material breach. § 5 is a pure revenue-share under which Kubient pays AP (sequential liability), with no AP-payable fee floor, and § 13 confirms no minimum revenue guarantee runs either way. § 7(a) further bars punitive and similar damages mutually. The Initial-Term restriction on termination in § 4(a) is a term/renewal point, not an AP-payable liquidated amount, and is not flagged here. No redline proposed.
